budget_items.topic: Article 3 - prior fiscal year expense (Haywood Hospital bill)
budget_items.what_was_said: The board noted a bill from Haywood Hospital to be paid from a prior fiscal year under article 3.

The consulting cost, funded from an unexpended capital project, is to help establish the process for a possible stormwater utility fee; a member objected that it commits money toward a foregone conclusion.

budget_items.topic: Article 5 - cable committee transfer of funds
budget_items.what_was_said: The transfer replicates a vote intended at annual town meeting once retained earnings were certified, plus an added appropriation for videographer funding.
The town manager told the finance committee the new vacation-bank language carries a financial impact, still being calculated ahead of their hearing.

decisions.decision: Job descriptions will be reviewed at minimum before the town seeks to fill a vacancy, not only upon an employee's exit.
Recommendations on annual cost-of-living increases will come from the town manager rather than the human resources director.
Language will specify the recommendation be presented at annual town meeting.
Board agreed to the concept of preserving a step-increase credit on promotion to a new grade, to be redrafted by labor counsel without a new board vote.
Sick leave language will change 'doctor's certificate' to 'doctor's note' and specify 'three consecutive days.'
Summary language will capitalize 'Town' only when referring to Lunenburg specifically, not when 'towns' is used generally.

minutes.summary: The Select Board worked through the remaining articles of the November 18 Special Town Meeting warrant, voting to include and recommend (or defer) articles on storm water consulting funding, a cable committee fund transfer, and several Salary Administration Plan amendments. Much of the meeting was a line-by-line review with labor counsel's redline changes to vacation-bank, sick-leave, grievance, and personnel-committee language, with several small wording fixes agreed without a formal revote.

what_happened.line: The board voted to recommend Article 16, rewriting Salary Administration Plan rules on vacation banking, sick leave, grievances and job descriptions.
Article 17, consolidating personnel-committee authority, passed 4-1 to recommend after review of labor counsel's changes.
The town manager told the finance committee the new vacation-bank language carries a financial impact still being calculated.
Article 4, funding storm water consulting from an unexpended capital project, was voted in, reconsidered, then re-voted after an objection.
Article 5, a cable committee fund transfer plus added videographer funding, passed unanimously to include and recommend.

why_it_matters: Articles 16 and 17 rewrite town personnel policy on vacation, sick leave and grievances -- residents vote on them at the Nov. 18 special town meeting.
The vacation-bank change carries a cost to the town that was not yet quantified when the finance committee took it up.
The storm water consulting article is a step toward a possible stormwater utility fee, a mechanism that could show up on future bills.

Finance committee hearing on the vacation-bank policy's financial impact

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on every vote after the Article 4 reconsideration, on the cable-committee transfer figures, and on most policy decisions discussed — but the official minutes report the very first Article 4 inclusion vote as "4-2-1," a tally that does not sum to the five members present and conflicts with our "4-1," and our attendee list is missing two of the five Select Board members named in the official record. A reader should also check the sick-leave language change, since the official minutes note the terms were "harmonized" without saying which term ("doctor's note" vs. "doctor's certificate") was kept, and whether the three-consecutive-day threshold was actually changed or just discussed.

findings.official: A motion to include Article 4 in the warrant was made, seconded, and passed 4-2-1.
findings.note: Official's 4-2-1 does not sum to the 5 members present and conflicts with our 4-1 reading; check the recording's roll call around t=148 — though this vote was superseded by the unanimous reconsideration and revote, so the practical outcome is not in question.

findings.about: scope of the job-description review requirement change (SAP Article 16)

findings.official: A transition mechanism was introduced whereby unused vacation time as of July 1, 2026, would be converted into a one-time vacation bank, with employees required to use at least one-third of that bank during each of fiscal years 2027, 2028, and 2029. Employees carrying balances over 120 hours as of June 30, 2026, would receive a lump-sum buyout of all time in excess of 120 hours.
findings.note: A substantive policy decision entirely absent from our minutes; worth confirming it was accurately captured for anyone relying on our record of Article 16.

findings.about: Personnel Committee quorum authority shifting to Select Board (SAP Section 70-12)
findings.official: Language was added providing that, in the event the Personnel Committee lacks sufficient members to conduct business, the Select Board shall have authority to administer the relevant provision of the SAP.
findings.note: Not captured in our minutes at all; a governance change worth noting for Article 16/17 context given the personnel committee is also the subject of Article 17.

findings.about: holiday pay clarifying language retained after discussion (SAP Section E)
findings.official: Labor counsel had struck clarifying language regarding the requirement to be in paid status on the day before and after a holiday in order to receive holiday pay. After discussion, the Select Board agreed the language should remain for clarity.
findings.note: A decision (to keep language labor counsel had proposed cutting) that is missing from our minutes.
